Let's analyze the options:

A. "Very few books are banned but an exception is a book by Jean Martin."  
This is vague and doesn't specify which book. Also, "Jean Martin" is not a well-known author in the context of Irish book bans.

B. "Books banned in Ireland include Catcher in the Rye, Brave New World and Ulysses."  
This is inaccurate. While Ireland had a history of banning books, most of these bans have been lifted. "Catcher in the Rye" and "Brave New World" were not banned in Ireland. "Ulysses" was banned for a time but is no longer banned.

C. "Catcher in the Rye by J.D. Salinger is banned."  
This is incorrect. "Catcher in the Rye" was never banned in Ireland.

D. "Balzac."  
This is too vague. Some works by Balzac were banned in the past, but not currently.

E. "Borstal Boy."  
This is interesting. "Borstal Boy" by Brendan Behan was banned in Ireland for obscenity, but the ban was lifted in 1970.

F. "Ulysses by James Joyce."  
"Ulysses" was banned in Ireland from 1922 until the 1960s, but the ban has since been lifted.

Currently, very few books are banned in Ireland. The Censorship of Publications Board still exists, but bans are rare and most classic bans have been lifted. The only answer that is accurate in the present tense is A, as it reflects the current situation: very few books are banned, and the only recent bans are obscure.

Answer: A
